v2:b0691cb10.claim: Tier-1 live data (§5.5, the whole of M1) cannot use the no-flash hold discipline §5.2 promises: the hold is gated on descriptor-node OBJECT identity, and `update(next: PlotHandle)` necessarily supplies fresh node objects, so every live tick drops the pane to the "Loading…" placeholder.
v2:b0691cb10.evidence: resolve-cache.ts:22-33 — `sourceKey` mints ids from a `WeakMap` on the node OBJECT (`idMap.get(obj)`), so a re-authored handle gets a brand-new key. plot-node.tsx:391-397 — the hold is `lastReadyRef.current?.base === baseKey` where `baseKey = sourceKey(node)`; a new node object ⇒ mismatch ⇒ `held === undefined` ⇒ `dataProps === undefined` ⇒ plot-node.tsx:407-408 sets status `"loading"` ⇒ plot-node.tsx:558-560 renders `<Message text="Loading…" />`. Scenario: host polls at 1 Hz, calls `cairnPlot.line(newData)` + `m.update(h2)`; every second the chart unmounts its renderer subtree and shows "Loading…", the exact opposite of spec lines 128-131 ("receives the new data via the hold discipline … no loading flash") and line 117 ("swaps in as a prop change (never a remount)"). Note the placeholder also unmounts the renderer subtree, which plot-node.tsx:268-274 documents as having already caused a real bug (enlarge state reset).
v2:b0691cb10.proposal: Stop keying resolution/hold on object identity. §5.2 must define a stable LEAF KEY that survives re-authoring: `(tree path, renderer, author-supplied key?)` — which also answers §9 Q1 — and §5.5 must state that the resolve key is `leafKey + contentRef`, not `sourceKey(node)`. Spell out that `update()` MUST carry the previous leaf's `lastReady` payload forward by leaf key, and add a harness gate asserting `__cairnLeafResolveStats.placeholderMounts` stays 0 across N `update()` calls (the counter at plot-node.tsx:199-215 already exists for exactly this).

v2:b0691cb10.claim: Nothing in the live-data path ever releases memory: the resolve cache, the runtime store, and the blob-URL cache are all append-only with no eviction, unregister, or revoke. A "live tracker" host running §5.5 Tier 1 or Tier 2 leaks every decoded frame it has ever shown until the tab dies.
v2:b0691cb10.evidence: resolve-cache.ts:41 `const cache = new Map<string, Entry<unknown>>()` — grep for `cache.delete` in resolve-cache.ts returns nothing; the only removal is `__resetResolveCacheForTest` (line 115-118, test seam). Keys are strings, so once the descriptor node is GC'd the WeakMap entry dies but the cached decoded payload stays reachable forever. runtime-store.ts:74-85 `registerRuntimeEntries` only `set`s into a page-level `window.__cairnPlotRuntimeStore`; there is no unregister. runtime-store.ts:96-115 `objectUrlCache` calls `URL.createObjectURL` and never revokes (repo-wide grep for `revokeObjectURL` hits only primitives/plot-to-png.ts:229). Scenario: a 1024×1024 RGBA f32 render card updated at 1 Hz retains 16 MB per tick in `cache` plus the raw buffer in the runtime store — ~1 GB in 60 s, tab OOM in minutes. §9 Q10 frames memory as a multi-mount dedup question; the real failure is a single mount over time.
v2:b0691cb10.proposal: Make lifetime part of the API contract, not an open question. §5.5 must specify: (a) a byte-budgeted LRU over the resolve cache with a configurable cap and a documented default; (b) `MountedPlot.update()` releases payloads for leaf keys no longer referenced, and `unmount()` releases all payloads it owns; (c) a `releaseRuntimeEntries(hashes)` companion to `registerRuntimeEntries` that also `URL.revokeObjectURL`s the cached blob URL; (d) `registerDataSource` entries are refcounted per ref so the last detaching viewport frees them. Add a memory-growth gate to the M1 exit criteria.

v2:b0691cb10.claim: The Tier-2 `subscribe(ref, onInvalidate)` hook is unimplementable against the cache the spec says it feeds, and §5.5's description of that cache as "content-keyed" is factually wrong — it is object-identity keyed, and it has no invalidation primitive at all.
v2:b0691cb10.evidence: Spec line 206-208 claims resolution "feeds the existing content-keyed subscribable resolve cache". resolve-cache.ts:11-15 says the opposite in its own doc: "`sourceKey` hands out that id via a `WeakMap` on the node OBJECT" — the key is node identity, and the module header line 3 states the design intent as "resolve … once, reuse it forever". resolve-cache.ts:83-84: `if (existing?.data !== undefined) return Promise.resolve(existing.data);` — once a key resolves, `run` is NEVER re-invoked. There is no exported evict/invalidate; plot-node.tsx:319 reinforces it (`if (peekResolved(key) !== undefined || peekResolveError(key) !== undefined) return;` — the leaf refuses to re-kick a resolved key). Scenario: adapter calls `onInvalidate()` for `track://run/17/loss`; cairn-plot has no API that can make the next `resolveCached` re-run `get()`, so the pane shows the first snapshot forever. The two claims are also mutually inconsistent: a truly content-keyed cache can never need invalidation; a ref-keyed cache is not content-keyed.
v2:b0691cb10.proposal: §5.5 must define the resolve key explicitly as `${ref}#${generation}`, with `generation` a monotonic per-ref counter cairn-plot owns; `onInvalidate(generation?)` bumps it, which naturally produces a new key (and lets "latest-wins coalescing" be defined as "only the highest generation is resolved; superseded in-flight resolves are dropped"). Add `evictRef(ref)` / bounded generation retention so old generations are collected (see LD2). Delete the word "content-keyed" from line 207 or make it true by keying on the adapter-supplied content key (see LD7).

v2:b0691cb10.claim: A single transient failure permanently bricks a live pane: resolve errors are cached with no expiry and the resolver is never re-invoked, so §9 Q9 ("adapter retry policy") is not an open question but a blocking gap.
v2:b0691cb10.evidence: resolve-cache.ts:86-100 — on rejection the entry keeps `data === undefined`, sets `entry.error`, and leaves `entry.promise` as an already-rejected promise. A later `resolveCached(key, run)` hits line 85 (`if (existing?.promise) return existing.promise.then(...)`) and returns that same rejected promise; `run` is never called again. prefetchResolved (line 106-111) only skips on `data !== undefined`, so it too just re-attaches to the dead promise. plot-node.tsx:319 short-circuits on `peekResolveError(key) !== undefined`, and plot-node.tsx:562-563 renders a terminal `Plot error: …`. Scenario: a tracker pane's `get()` fails once during a server restart; the pane displays "Plot error" for the rest of the session even after the server returns and `onInvalidate` fires — because the new generation is the only escape and LD3 shows that path does not exist.
v2:b0691cb10.proposal: §5.5 must specify error semantics: cached errors are TRANSIENT entries with a documented backoff (e.g. exponential to a cap) after which the next read re-invokes `get`; add `Viewport.onError(cb)` and an explicit `Viewport.retry()` to the §5.3 interface so a host can drive its own retry UI; state that an errored ref never blocks a subsequent invalidation from re-resolving. Also state whether the last good frame is held through an error (today it is not — plot-node.tsx:394 drops the hold as soon as `cacheError !== undefined`), which for a live tracker is almost certainly the wrong default.

v2:b0691cb10.claim: `get(ref, { signal })` has no defined owner and is incompatible with the sharing/coalescing the same section relies on: one `run()` is shared by N consumers, so any consumer's abort corrupts the shared entry for everyone — and under the StrictMode guarantee of §5.6 the very first resolve is the one that gets aborted.
v2:b0691cb10.evidence: resolve-cache.ts:82-101 — `resolveCached` runs `run()` exactly once per key and every subsequent caller attaches to `entry.promise`; there is no refcount and no way to signal "this caller went away". plot-node.tsx:328-332/357-359 shows the current stand-in: the cleanup only sets a local `cancelled` flag and lets the resolve run to completion — i.e. no cancellation exists today, and the spec introduces a signal without saying who aborts it. Scenario A (StrictMode, spec line 228): React double-invokes the effect — mount, cleanup, mount. If cleanup aborts, the first `get` rejects with AbortError, which LD4 shows is cached permanently; the remount reads the poisoned entry and renders "Plot error: The operation was aborted". Scenario B: two panes show the same ref; one is unmounted by an `update()` that changes its renderer (spec line 132); its abort kills the in-flight fetch the still-mounted pane was coalescing onto.
v2:b0691cb10.proposal: §5.5 must state the ownership rule: cairn-plot refcounts consumers per resolve key, creates ONE AbortController per key, and aborts only when the refcount reaches zero AND the entry is still in flight; AbortError is never cached as an error state (the entry is deleted so the next consumer re-resolves). Alternatively drop `signal` from the v1 contract and let the adapter own cancellation — but say which, because "opts: { signal }" as written implies a per-call lifetime the cache cannot provide.

v2:b0691cb10.claim: "`DataPayload` mirrors the runtime-store entry union" (line 211-212) is factually wrong — that union has exactly two members, neither of which covers most of the listed kinds — so §9 Q6 is asking about the completeness of a type that does not exist.
v2:b0691cb10.evidence: runtime-store.ts:30-50 — the union is exactly `RuntimeBytesEntry { kind:"bytes"; bytes; mime }` | `RuntimeFloatEntry { kind:"float"; data; shape; dtype; precision }`. The spec's "npy array, table blob, mesh/pointcloud/volume/boxes payloads" have no runtime-store representation at all; they are resolved by separate fetch+parse functions over `DataSource.bytes` — data-sources.ts:305-320 (`fetchPointCloudArrays`), :342-356 (`fetchMeshArrays`), :364-371 (`fetchVolumeArray`), :384-396 (`fetchBoxesArrays`). Worse, the two shapes are not interchangeable: runtime-store.ts:103-109 `runtimeArtifactUrl` THROWS for a float entry ("resolve it via the float-source path … not artifactUrl()"), so a data source returning a float DataPayload cannot be consumed by any code path that expects a URL (e.g. data-sources.ts:127-131, `resolveImageViewportItems`).
v2:b0691cb10.proposal: Define `DataPayload` in the spec as its own explicit tagged union — one variant per supported content kind (`bytes`, `float`, `npyArray`, `table`, `mesh`, `pointcloud`, `volume`, `boxes`), each carrying a required `contentKey` — and state which viewport kinds accept which variants. Drop the "mirrors the runtime-store union" sentence; instead specify the ADAPTER from `DataPayload` into the runtime store / DataSource seam, and note that the float variant is URL-unrepresentable.

v2:b0691cb10.claim: §5.5's promise that "unchanged content = no re-decode/re-upload" fails for exactly the refs live data cares about: a `track://…@latest` ref has no content identity, and the runtime path mints a fresh RANDOM id per registration, so every invalidation is a full re-decode, re-upload, and re-diff even when the bytes are byte-identical.
v2:b0691cb10.evidence: runtime-store.ts:117-126 — `mintRuntimeHash` returns `runtime:${counter}-${random}`, explicitly documented as "Uniqueness — not content-addressing". The GPU compare/diff caches key on content keys, not on the node: plot-node.tsx:445-446 (`contentKeyA: dp.__diffContentKeyA`, `contentKeyB: …`) and plot-node.tsx:748-751 `frameContentKey` = `float.contentKey ?? url`. The only mechanism that gives a mutable live URL a stable content key today is redirect-following — plot-node.tsx:601-604 and data-sources.ts:200-208 ("The FINAL post-redirect url is the stable diff-cache content key (a live query url that redirects to a content-addressed digest keys on the digest)"). A `track://` ref resolved by a registered adapter never goes through `fetch`, so no digest is recovered and `DataPayload` (per LD6) carries no `contentKey` field. Scenario: an image card on `track://run/17/render@latest` polling every 2 s while the run is idle re-uploads an unchanged rgba32float texture and re-runs the FLIP kernel on every tick.
v2:b0691cb10.proposal: Make `contentKey` (adapter-supplied etag/digest, opaque string) a REQUIRED field of every `DataPayload`, and specify that cairn-plot: (a) short-circuits an invalidation whose new payload carries the same `contentKey` as the current one — no re-decode, no re-upload, no re-render; (b) keys decode/GPU-upload/diff caches on `contentKey` rather than on ref or node identity. Also state what happens when an adapter cannot supply one (documented degraded path: always re-decode), so the guarantee on line 207 is conditional and honest.

v2:b0691cb10.claim: "`cairnPlot.line({ src: \"track://run/17/loss\" }); // grows live" (line 200) has no incremental path: every payload shape in play is a whole buffer, so an appending series is re-fetched, re-parsed and re-uploaded in full on every invalidation — O(n) per tick, O(n²) over a run.
v2:b0691cb10.evidence: Both candidate unions are whole-buffer only: runtime-store.ts:31-48 (`bytes: ArrayBuffer` / `data: Float32Array|Uint16Array` + `shape`), and the parse helpers materialize whole arrays each time — data-sources.ts:305-320, :364-371 (`Float32Array.from(...)` over the entire parsed blob). The resolve cache has no notion of a partial or extended entry (resolve-cache.ts:35-39 `Entry<T> { data?; error?; promise? }`). Combined with LD3's generation keying, each tick allocates a full new entry that LD2 shows is never freed. Scenario: a 10 Hz training run for one hour ⇒ 36k-point series; the last tick alone re-transfers and re-parses all 36k points, and the session has retained ~36k separate whole-series copies.
v2:b0691cb10.proposal: Either (a) add an append variant to `DataPayload` — `{ kind: "append", ref, generation, sinceIndex, values }` — with a spec'd rule that cairn-plot concatenates into the existing entry in place (and how a gap/reset forces a full re-fetch), or (b) explicitly scope Tier 2 to whole-snapshot refs in §5.5 and state the resulting cost model plus a documented series-length ceiling, so hosts don't discover the quadratic behavior in production. Given goal 3 ("Live data as a first-class concern (cairn-track is a live tracker)"), (a) is the one that meets the stated goal.

v2:c6a1eadd6.claim: §5.7 says the registered module shape "is today's `ViewportModule`", but `ViewportModule` is a CARD-level contract, not a pane contract — nothing in the descriptor mount path can play the card, so `registerViewport` is unimplementable as written.
v2:c6a1eadd6.evidence: `ViewportModule.useData(args)` takes ARRAYS across a card's pane list and returns arrays (`viewport/types.ts:163-208`: `hashes: (string|null)[]`, `referenceHashes`, `metadata`, `mimes`; result `items`/`referenceItems` "index-aligned with the card's pane list"). `activeColorbar` is explicitly card-level: "VisualContentCard calls this ONCE per render (never per-Pane)" (`types.ts:435`, `:322-331`). `capabilities.maxPanes` / `webglContextsPerPane` are budgets "the card should enforce" (`types.ts:118-126`), and `capabilities` as a whole exists so "VisualContentCard reads this to decide which chrome to render" (`types.ts:75-82`). `ViewportPaneProps` requires ~30 card-supplied fields — `mode`, `diffMode`, `diffKernel`, `splitPosition`/`onSplitPositionChange`, `label`, `isBaseline`, `isDraggable`/`onDragStart`, `crossTypeReferenceUrl`, `crossTypeAlignForDiff`, `cameraSyncGroupId`, `colorRange` (`types.ts:218-339`). The descriptor path has no such caller: it resolves ONE leaf per node through `registerRenderer(name, ComponentType<any>)` (`ui/src/plot-registry.tsx:36`) with a flat prop bag from `resolveDataProps` (`ui/src/plot-renderers.tsx:68-69, 428-437`). §5.7 never says who calls `useData` with which hashes, who supplies `mode`/`splitPosition`/`label`, or who renders the single colorbar.
v2:c6a1eadd6.proposal: Do not re-export `ViewportModule` as the registration shape. Define a NEW per-leaf `PaneModule` in §5.7: `{ id, defaultSettings(), migrateSettings?, Pane: ComponentType<{ data, settings, view, onViewChange, size }> , capabilities: {settingsKeys, screenshot} }` — singular data, no reference/compare/cross-type/colorbar chrome (compare stays a `compare` descriptor node). If the card-shaped contract must survive for cairn-track's 3D cards, say explicitly that it is NOT descriptor-mountable and stays a private app-side path until M3 deletes it.

v2:c6a1eadd6.claim: A custom viewport cannot get at host data: `ViewportModule.useData` is a React HOOK designed to run inside the host's provider tree, but §5.6 rules that host React context does not cross into the plot root. Any real `registerViewport` module throws at first render.
v2:c6a1eadd6.evidence: `viewport/types.ts:355-360`: useData "May be backed by react-query internally (3D's npz fetch); image's implementation ... is composed at the app layer because it calls `api.artifactUrl`". The shipped implementations confirm it: `cairn/ui/src/components/viewport-registry.tsx:1-16,60,74-80` builds `useImageData` from `api.artifactUrl` + `createEndpointDataSource`, and the 3D modules do the same inside card files (`MeshVisualCard.tsx:512`, `VolumeVisualCard.tsx:523`). §5.6 states "Own React root inside the host tree (host context does NOT cross)". Failing scenario: cairn-track calls `registerViewport("track-trace", m)` where `m.useData` calls `useQuery`; `<Plot handle={h}/>` creates its own root; the module's hook executes there; `QueryClientProvider` is in the host tree → "No QueryClient set, use QueryClientProvider" on first paint of every custom pane. The same applies to any host context (auth, theme, api client).
v2:c6a1eadd6.proposal: Pick one and specify it: (a) forbid hooks in the module — a custom pane obtains data ONLY through `registerDataSource` (§5.5, async, React-free) and receives resolved `DataPayload` as a prop; or (b) add an explicit provider seam to §5.6 (`<Plot providers={Wrapper}>` / `mount(el, {wrapper})`) that the plot root renders around every pane, and state the StrictMode/identity rules for it. Option (a) is consistent with the rest of the spec; (b) reintroduces the coupling §1 is removing.

v2:c6a1eadd6.claim: §5.7 creates a SECOND registry for the same descriptor field (`renderer`), colliding with the existing `registerRenderer` registry that actually drives descriptor resolution and the addon-loading protocol.
v2:c6a1eadd6.evidence: Descriptor `renderer` names resolve through `getRenderer(name)` in the module-singleton registry (`ui/src/plot-registry.tsx:31-59`), seeded by `registerCoreRenderers()` (`ui/src/plot-renderers.tsx:440-444`) and extended at runtime by addon IIFEs via `window.__cairnPlotRegisterRenderer` (`ui/src/plot-bootstrap.tsx:277`), with an `onRegister` wait-for-registration path for "renderer not yet registered" (`plot-registry.tsx:24-29`). §5.7's example — `registerViewport("track-trace", module); // descriptors may then use { kind: "plot", renderer: "track-trace" }` — targets the same namespace with an incompatible value type. Failing scenario: a page mounts `{kind:"plot", renderer:"track-trace"}`; `getRenderer("track-trace")` returns undefined because the module went into the other registry, so the bootstrap sits in its bounded wait and then errors "unknown renderer". Symmetrically, `registerViewport("image", …)` and `registerRenderer("image", …)` can both "win" with no defined precedence.
v2:c6a1eadd6.proposal: One namespace, one lookup. Either `registerViewport` internally adapts the module to a `ComponentType` and writes into the SAME registry (specify the adapter and shadowing rules for core names), or give custom panes their own descriptor discriminant (`{kind:"viewport", module:"track-trace"}`) so the two resolution paths never contend. Also state whether the window hook remains the addon protocol for custom viewports in offline bundles.

v2:c6a1eadd6.claim: Custom viewports do NOT get settings/layers/sync "for free" — the entire layer machinery is hardcoded to the IMAGE settings vocabulary, and compare/selection eligibility is a hardcoded renderer-name set. §5.3's claim that `ViewportSettings` is "a discriminated union ... the SAME shapes the settings stores hold internally" describes a union of exactly one member.
v2:c6a1eadd6.evidence: `viewport/image-settings-sync.ts:41-85` — the ONLY settings payload type is `ImageSyncSettings` (encoding, tonemapGamma, peak, exposureEV, offset, colorMin/Max, compareMode, diffKernel, splitPosition, channelSelect, infoPanel). Layers are not objects: `:166 export type SettingsLayerStack = readonly string[]` (group-id strings), `:170 pushSettingsLayer(stack, layerId)`, `:212 resolveSettingsStack(stack): ImageSyncSettings | null`, backed by a process-global bus keyed by group id (`:109-115`). Consumers are image-only: `renderers/CpuImagePane.tsx`, `renderers/GpuImagePane.tsx`, `media-compare/compositor.tsx`, `plot-node.tsx`, `plot-selection-stage.tsx` — no chart, no 3D. Compare/selection eligibility is a literal name set: `ui/src/plot-selection-pane-registry.ts:25 const IMAGE_RENDERERS = new Set(["image","imagehdr"])`, `:29-33 isImageCompatibleNode`. Failing scenario: `registerViewport("track-trace")`; the pane gets `pushSettingsLayer([`vp-st-${paneId}`], groups?.settingsGroupId)` (`plot-node.tsx:1038`) whose resolved value is typed `ImageSyncSettings`, so its own settings have no representation; and it can never be selected into a compare/enlarge group. Charts are worse: `ScalarPlotStandalone` holds its interactive state in component-local `useState` (`plot-renderers.tsx:170-176`) with NO store at all — yet M1 migrates ScalarPlotCard first, whose settings are exactly those chart fields (`cairn/ui/src/components/ScalarPlotCard.tsx:48-67`). `getSettings()`/`setSettings()` on a scalar pane has nothing to read or write today.
v2:c6a1eadd6.proposal: Make the layer store generic over an opaque per-kind bag: key the bus by `(kind, layerId)` and type values as `unknown`/`TSettings` with the registration declaring `settingsSchema`+`defaults`+`migrate`. Replace `IMAGE_RENDERERS` with a module-declared capability (`comparable: boolean`, `compareSpace: "raster" | none`). And add a milestone before M1 that gives CHART leaves a real settings store — otherwise §5.3 is undeliverable for the first card migrated.

v2:c6a1eadd6.claim: `Viewport` in §5.3/§4 collides head-on with the already-public `Viewport` type (the axis window) and with two other in-repo meanings of the word; the API will ship a viewport whose settings contain a `viewport`.
v2:c6a1eadd6.evidence: `ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/types.ts:44 export interface Viewport { xMin; xMax; yMin; yMax }`, re-exported publicly at `ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/index.ts:22`, consumed as a descriptor-visible prop name (`plot-renderers.tsx:52,171-191` — `p.viewport`, `onViewportChange`) and persisted as a CARD SETTINGS KEY in the very card M1 migrates (`cairn/ui/src/components/ScalarPlotCard.tsx:61-66 viewport: {xMin,xMax,yMin,yMax}`). Meanwhile `viewport/types.ts` uses "Viewport" for the pane module (`ViewportModule`, `ViewportPaneProps`), `viewportSyncGroupId` means the zoom/pan bus (`plot-node.tsx:1118`, `renderers/use-synced-image-viewport.ts`), and §4 adds a third meaning — the mounted pane handle — exported from the SAME entry as the axis-window type. Result: `import type { Viewport } from "cairn-plot"` is ambiguous by construction, and the migrated code reads `vp.getSettings().viewport.xMin`.
v2:c6a1eadd6.proposal: Rename the mounted-pane handle to `Pane` (`MountedPlot.panes`, `plot.pane`, `PaneSettings`, `pushLayer` on `Pane`) and the entry point to `cairn-plot/panes`; reserve "viewport" exclusively for the axis/zoom window it already denotes on the wire. Add a §4 note that `Viewport` (axis window) stays exported from `cairn-plot` unchanged.

v2:c6a1eadd6.claim: `Viewport.id = descriptor tree path` is not the key settings are stored under, so the §5.2 preservation guarantee is unbacked, layer addressing is ambiguous while a pane is staged/enlarged, and layers are never released.
v2:c6a1eadd6.evidence: The pane's identity today is an ephemeral counter, not a path: `plot-node.tsx:937 const [paneId] = useState(nextSelectionPaneId)` → `viewport/selection-store.ts:341-343 return `cp-pane-${paneSeq++}``; the viewport-local settings layer is `vp-st-${paneId}` (`plot-node.tsx:1038`). Nothing maps descriptor path → paneId. (a) Any React remount mints a new paneId and silently resets that pane's settings, contradicting §5.2 "a leaf whose (path, renderer) is unchanged keeps its viewport (settings intact)". (b) The enlarge/compare stage renders a SECOND live instance of the same descriptor path from the pane registry (`ui/src/plot-selection-pane-registry.ts:1-14` — "the stage reads the registry ... and renders FRESH leaves via `PlotNodeView`"), with its own paneId and its own `vp-st-*` layer; §5.3's path-addressed `setSettings`/`pushLayer`/`screenshot()` do not say which instance they hit. (c) Nothing frees a layer: `clearImageSettings` is called only on selection-group formation (`renderers/use-synced-image-settings.ts:124`), so the global `lastStates` + `versions` maps (`image-settings-sync.ts:109-115,193-200`) accumulate one entry per pane instance for the process lifetime — unbounded for a live tracker that remounts panes.
v2:c6a1eadd6.proposal: Specify a stable pane identity: author-supplied `key` on descriptor leaves (answers open question 1) falling back to `path + renderer`, and key the settings store on it instead of `nextSelectionPaneId`. Define stage semantics explicitly (the staged instance IS the same `Pane` — it inherits the local layer; transients stack above it). Add `layer.dispose()` / release-on-last-detach to §5.4 and a note that `SettingsLayer` ids are process-global.

v2:c6a1eadd6.claim: The "experimental, hosts pin the submodule" exemption (§8) provides no protection under the stated consumption model, and publishing `ViewportModule` re-exports exactly the internals §6 declares private.
v2:c6a1eadd6.evidence: §3 non-goals keep consumption "source-compiled via the submodule", i.e. ONE pin covering all three entries — there is no way to take a `cairn-plot` bump while holding `cairn-plot/viewport` at an older revision, so the exemption reduces to "this part will keep breaking your typecheck on every bump", which is the exact pain §1 exists to remove. It is not a marginal path: today's app-specific panes ARE `ViewportModule`s (`cairn/ui/src/components/viewport-registry.tsx:277`, `MeshVisualCard.tsx:512`, `VolumeVisualCard.tsx:523`, `PointCloudVisualCard.tsx`), and §7 M4 turns deep imports into lint errors while leaving this as the only escape hatch. Separately, `viewport/types.ts:1-4` imports `ColormapName`/`DiffMode` from `../types`, `MediaCompareModeKind` from `../media-compare/mode`, and `CompareFloatSource` from `../media-compare/compositor` — and `CompareFloatSource`/`MediaCompareModeKind`/`DiffMode` appear in the public shape (`types.ts:229-247`). §6 puts `media-compare` internals (`OffscreenComparePanes`, compositor) on the private list. Exporting `ViewportModule` therefore either leaks the private surface or fails to typecheck at the boundary.
v2:c6a1eadd6.proposal: State the real guarantee: `cairn-plot/viewport` breaks on bumps, and cairn-track owns the adoption cost — plus a concrete bound (e.g. "a ViewportModule change lands with a codemod and one milestone of shim"). And retype the exported contract against PUBLIC types only (a `PaneModule` whose props reference `DataPayload`, `ViewportSettings`, and public colormap/diff enums), so §6's privacy list and §4's export list are consistent.

v2:c6a1eadd6.claim: `getSettings(): ViewportSettings` / `setSettings(patch: Partial<ViewportSettings>)` over a discriminated union is not type-safe: `Partial<Union>` drops the discriminant and admits cross-kind key mixes, and `Viewport.kind: string` gives callers no narrowing.
v2:c6a1eadd6.evidence: §5.3 declares `kind: string` and `ViewportSettings` as "a discriminated union by `kind` (image settings, mesh view state, ...)". With TS's distributive behavior, `Partial<A|B>` accepts `{colormap: "turbo", position: [0,0,0]}` — an image key plus a camera key — and a host must cast on every read because `kind` is a bare `string`. The existing modules are already generic per kind for exactly this reason (`viewport/types.ts:347-352 ViewportModule<TData, TView extends ViewState, TSettings, M>` and `ViewState`'s explicit `kind` discriminant at `:54-61`). Open question 7 in the spec is downstream of this same gap.
v2:c6a1eadd6.proposal: Make the handle generic: `Pane<K extends PaneKind = PaneKind>` with `kind: K`, `getSettings(): SettingsFor<K>`, `setSettings(p: Partial<SettingsFor<K>>)`, plus a narrowing helper (`pane.as("image")` returning `Pane<"image"> | null`). Custom (`registerViewport`) kinds map to `SettingsFor<string> = Record<string, unknown>` so they are opt-in unsafe rather than making the whole union unsafe.

v2:314b009fe.claim: The API has no channel for interaction events. §5.3/§5.6 expose exactly `onSettingsChange` and `onReady`, but the cards being migrated are driven by pane→host callbacks that are NOT settings changes. Every one of them becomes unimplementable the moment deep imports are lint-blocked (§4).
v2:314b009fe.evidence: cairn/ui/src/components/ScatterPlotCard.tsx:258-259 passes `onClick: (id) => toggle(id)` and `onBackgroundClick: clear` — clicking a scatter point toggles the page-wide RUN selection. cairn/ui/src/components/ScalarPlotCard.tsx:552-555 passes `onSeriesClick: (key) => { const rid = seriesKeyToRunId.get(key); if (rid) toggle(rid); }`. cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/renderers/ScatterPlot.tsx:43,134,146 exposes `onHover(pointId, anchor)` (drives the host tooltip/inspector). cairn-plot/.../renderers/ImagePaneShell.tsx:315,785 and renderers/image-backend.ts:181,406,572 thread a host `onDragStart` into the pane's LabelChip; cairn/ui/src/components/card-kit/MultiPaneGrid.tsx:20 names that drag source (`startViewportDrag`, `CAIRN_IMAGE_MIME`) and cairn/ui/src/components/card-kit/use-reference-drop.ts:14-20,77 consumes the dropped payload to establish a GLOBAL comparison reference. Failing scenario: M1 migrates ScalarPlotCard per §7; the descriptor carries series, `Viewport.onSettingsChange` fires for colormap/viewport keys, and there is no event on which `onSeriesClick` can be rebuilt — clicking a legend entry can no longer select a run. Same for M4's ScatterPlotCard and M2's image cards' drag-out-as-reference.
v2:314b009fe.proposal: Add a typed event channel alongside settings: `Viewport.on(type, cb): () => void` with a closed union — `"pick"` ({datumId, seriesKey, x, y, modifiers}), `"backgroundclick"`, `"hover"` ({datumId|null, clientAnchor}), `"dragstart"` ({nativeEvent}) — plus per-leaf host-supplied presentation the host can no longer inject (`label`, `draggable`) as descriptor fields. Mirror it on `<Plot onEvent={(vp, ev) => …}>`. State the rule explicitly: settings = persisted display state, events = transient user intent; anything a card does with a click that is not a settings write goes through events.

v2:314b009fe.claim: Pane selection and reference-pick — a DOCUMENT-SCOPED module singleton in cairn-plot — is invisible and uncontrollable from the Host API. §5.4 leans on it ('selection episode', 'in-page transients always sit ABOVE host layers') while giving the host no way to read it, write it, or scope it to one mount. Two independent MountedPlots on one page silently share one selection set.
v2:314b009fe.evidence: cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/viewport/selection-store.ts:1-27 — 'ONE page-wide selection set … obtains the SAME document-scoped store (getGlobalSelectionStore)… a selection can span independent React roots'. selection-store.ts:110-122 `reference()` and :129-136 `setReference(id)` designate the pane every comparison is taken against; :86-98 `select(id, mode)` with replace/toggle; :167-180 `remove`/`prune` on unmount; :56-60 `StageMode = "enlarge"|"compare"` requests a page-level fullscreen stage. None of this appears anywhere in §5. Failing scenario: a cairn-track board holds a ScalarPlotCard for run A and an image card for run B, each its own `h.mount(el)`. The user shift-clicks two panes inside card B to form a compare group; the selection store is page-wide, so card A's panes are in the same id space and the host has no `scope` to prevent a stray click in A from collapsing B's group (`select(id,"replace")` clears everything). Second scenario: cairn-track already owns a reference concept (card-kit/use-media-reference.ts `MediaReferenceTag`, `globalHash`, `perPaneHash`) and must keep it in sync with cairn-plot's `reference()` — with no read, no write, and no change event, the two reference notions permanently diverge.
v2:314b009fe.proposal: Make selection a first-class part of the host boundary: `MountedPlot.getSelection(): {panes: string[], reference: string|null}`, `setSelection(...)`, `setReference(id)`, `onSelectionChange(cb)`, and a mount option `selectionScope: "page" | "mount" | SelectionScopeHandle` (default `"mount"` for hosts; `"page"` reproduces today's baked-gallery behavior). Also expose or suppress the stage request (`onStageRequest(mode)` / `stage: false`) so a host that owns its own fullscreen modal is not fighting a body-portaled one.

v2:314b009fe.claim: There is no disposal API anywhere in the spec, and the mechanisms §5.5 Tier 1 depends on retain everything forever on `window`. `update()` at ~Hz — the explicitly blessed live path — leaks monotonically and survives `unmount()`. §5.5's 'unchanged content = no re-decode/re-upload' is also false for Tier-1 runtime data.
v2:314b009fe.evidence: cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/viewport/runtime-store.ts: the registry is `window.__cairnPlotRuntimeStore` (storeOrNull()); `registerRuntimeEntries` only ever calls `store.set(hash, entry)` — there is no `delete` in the file; `objectUrlCache` calls `URL.createObjectURL` and never `revokeObjectURL` (grep for `revokeObjectURL` across runtime-store.ts/local-store.ts/resolve-cache.ts returns nothing). Critically `mintRuntimeHash()` documents 'Uniqueness — not content-addressing … a fresh id per registration' — so a re-authored handle carrying byte-identical data gets a NEW hash. resolve-cache.ts keys on `sourceKey(node)` and holds `const cache = new Map<string, Entry<unknown>>()` with no eviction. builder/handle.ts `MountedPlot` is `{element, unmount}` and `unmount` only tears down the React root — it never touches the runtime store. Failing scenario: ScalarPlotCard on Tier-1 (M1) polls at 1 Hz and calls `m.update(h2)`; a 1024×1024 f32 image card doing the same retains ~4 MB per tick on the page-level Map — ~14 GB/hour, not freed by closing the card. Second scenario: identical bytes on two consecutive ticks produce two hashes ⇒ two `sourceKey`s ⇒ full re-decode and re-upload every tick, contradicting §5.5's caching claim and Goal 4.
v2:314b009fe.proposal: Add explicit lifetime: `PlotHandle.dispose()` (drops its runtime entries + revokes its blob URLs), `MountedPlot.unmount()` disposes handles it exclusively owns, and make ownership counted so §9-Q10 (multiple mounts sharing data) is answered by refcount rather than left open. Make `mintRuntimeHash` content-addressed (hash the bytes) so re-authoring identical data is a cache hit — otherwise Tier 1 cannot deliver the stated no-flash/no-re-upload behavior. Give the resolve cache a documented budget (byte cap + LRU) and expose `configureCache({maxBytes})`.

v2:314b009fe.claim: View state (image zoom/pan, 3D camera, chart viewport) is not in `ViewportSettings` and has no API of its own — so linking zoom across two mounted cards is unreachable, and the first migration target loses a behavior it has today.
v2:314b009fe.evidence: §5.3 defines `ViewportSettings` as 'the SAME shapes the settings stores hold internally'. cairn-plot/.../viewport/image-settings-sync.ts:36-90 enumerates that shape exhaustively — encoding, tonemapGamma, peak, exposureEV, offset, norm, reduce, colorMin/Max, compareMode, diffKernel, splitPosition, channelSelect, info-panel visibility — and contains NO zoom/pan. Zoom/pan lives on a *separate* bus: viewport/image-viewport-sync.ts:1-12 ('the IMAGE mirror of three/camera-sync.ts's 3D camera bus. One EventTarget per groupId'), and selection-store.ts:9-14 confirms the React layer threads *two* group ids (`image-viewport-sync` and `image-settings-sync`) into selected panes. §5.2's own prose ('keep their instances, settings, zoom') treats zoom as distinct from settings. So §5.4 layers — the spec's only sharing primitive — cannot express 'link zoom between card A and card B', which is exactly the cross-mount feature the library already implements internally. Regression scenario: cairn/ui/src/components/ScalarPlotCard.tsx:542-544 passes `viewport: settings.viewport` and `onViewportChange: (v) => updateSettings({viewport: v})` — the card persists and restores the chart viewport today. After M1 there is no `getView`/`setView`/`onViewChange`, so a card cannot restore the user's zoom on reload.
v2:314b009fe.proposal: Either fold view state into `ViewportSettings` as a documented per-kind `view` sub-object (and say so in §5.3, since it changes the persistence and layer-sharing story), or add a parallel triple `Viewport.getView()/setView(v)/onViewChange(cb)` plus an explicit cross-mount primitive `linkViews(viewports, {zoom, pan, camera}): Disposable` that wraps the existing group-id buses. Answer whether a layer shared across two *mounts* is legal at all (§5.4 only describes layers within a mount).

v2:314b009fe.claim: The styling/theme contract is absent from §4's entry-point table and §5.6 states the wrong mechanism. A host that obeys §4 literally ('exactly three module entry points… everything else is private') renders unstyled, mis-themed panes.
v2:314b009fe.evidence: cairn/ui/tailwind.config.ts imports `../../vendor/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/tailwind-preset` as a preset AND globs `"../../vendor/cairn-plot/ui/src/**/*.{ts,tsx}"` into `content` with the comment 'Scan the app source AND the vendored cairn-plot renderer source so Tailwind keeps the utility classes the renderers use (otherwise they'd be purged)'. So the real public surface includes (a) the preset module and (b) a build-time dependency on the entire *private* source tree — neither is in §4, and neither is covered by §8's versioning discipline. Theme mismatch: tailwind-preset.ts:23 sets `darkMode: "class"` and cairn/ui/tailwind.config.ts repeats `darkMode: "class"`, i.e. dark styling keys off a `.dark` ancestor class. §5.6 claims 'theme via DOM `data-theme`'. Grepping the library, `data-theme` appears only in primitives/themed-portal.ts:105-108 (copying the attribute onto body portals) and one browser test — nothing styles off it. A host following §5.6 and setting `data-theme="dark"` gets light panes. Renderer components hard-depend on preset tokens (viewport/ViewportPlaceholder.tsx:25-27 uses `text-fg-muted`, `bg-bg`).
v2:314b009fe.proposal: Add a fourth entry to §4: `cairn-plot/styles` exporting the Tailwind preset plus a prebuilt CSS file for hosts that do not run Tailwind, and document the content-glob requirement as part of the contract (or eliminate it by shipping compiled CSS, which is the only way §4's 'everything else is private' is honest). Fix §5.6 to say the actual mechanism (`.dark` class per `darkMode:"class"`) or change the preset to `darkMode: ["class", '[data-theme="dark"]']` and state that both work.

v2:314b009fe.claim: No loading/error/staleness surface exists (§9-Q9 flags it and §5 answers nothing), and §5.2's hold discipline actively makes a failed live fetch indistinguishable from healthy live data — a correctness hazard for a live tracker, not a polish item.
v2:314b009fe.evidence: §5.2: 'previous frame shown until the new payload resolves — no loading flash'; §5.5: 'On invalidation the pane holds its current frame until the new payload is decoded.' The resolve cache does track failure — cairn-plot/.../resolve-cache.ts `interface Entry<T> { data?; error?: string; promise? }` — and 3D panes render an internal chip (viewport/ViewportPlaceholder.tsx:17-27, variants `empty`/`loading`/`error`), but neither is reachable from `Viewport`. Failing scenario: a Tier-2 ref `track://run/17/render@latest` starts 404-ing because the run was archived mid-session. `get()` rejects, the resolve entry records `error`, and per the hold rule the pane keeps painting the last good frame forever. The card header shows no error, no retry, no 'stale as of 14:02'; the user reads a stale render as the current step. Second scenario: a slow first-load ref on a cold pane — the host card cannot show its own skeleton, because it has no way to know a resolve is in flight.
v2:314b009fe.proposal: Add `Viewport.getStatus(): { state: "empty"|"loading"|"ready"|"stale"|"error", ref?: string, error?: Error, resolvedAt?: number }` and `onStatusChange(cb)`, surfaced on the React adapter as `onStatus`. Specify that the hold discipline is bounded: after a host-configurable `staleAfterMs` the viewport reports `"stale"` (host decides the visual). Add `render: "host"` so a host that shows its own error/empty UI can suppress the internal placeholder.

v2:314b009fe.claim: There is no host testing story without a GPU. §9-Q8 names the problem and §7's milestone gates are cairn-plot's gates, not the host's — yet §6 privatizes precisely the pure, DOM-cheap renderers that make host card tests possible today.
v2:314b009fe.evidence: cairn-plot/ui/package.json: `"test": "node --experimental-strip-types --test 'src/lib/cairn-plot/**/*.test.ts'"` (framework-free modules only) and a separate `"test:harness"` — every renderer-level test is a real-browser `.browser.ts` (renderers/__tests__ contains gpu-image-pane.browser.ts, engine-fallback.browser.ts, selection-stage.browser.ts, page-wide-selection.browser.ts, …). §6 makes `ScalarPlot`, `BarChart`, `ImageViewportPane`, `parseNpy`/`parseNpz`, `table-diff` and the series utils (`emaSmooth`, `filterOutliers`) private; those are exactly the pure functions/SVG components a host can exercise without a canvas. After migration the only host-reachable path is `h.mount(el)` → a real React root → canvas/WebGPU. Compounding it: the memory note 'WebGPU secure-context gating' documents that `navigator.gpu` is hidden on plain-HTTP LAN origins and panes silently degrade — and the spec exposes no capability query, so neither a host test nor a host runtime can ask 'will this render, and with which backend?' (cairn-plot answers this today only by injecting a vanilla DOM banner: primitives/capability-notice.ts:1-45). §7's M1-M4 gates never mention a host-side test gate at all.
v2:314b009fe.proposal: Add a fourth entry point `cairn-plot/testing`: a headless mounter with a stub backend that resolves descriptors, applies settings, and exposes the resolved per-viewport state for assertions without WebGPU/canvas; plus pure descriptor helpers (`validateDescriptor`, `resolveSettings(stack)`) so layer/merge semantics are unit-testable. Separately add `getCapabilities(): { webgpu: boolean, reason?: "insecure-origin"|"unsupported", hdr: boolean }` on the public entry so hosts can branch and so §9-Q5's HDR screenshot question has an input. Make 'cairn-track card tests still run headless' an explicit M1 exit gate in §7.

v2:314b009fe.claim: The API defines no keyboard/focus ownership, while the library installs window/document-level capture-phase handlers that call `stopPropagation()` — so mounted plots silently eat the host's Escape and outside-click handling, and N mounted cards install N handlers.
v2:314b009fe.evidence: cairn-plot/.../primitives/FullscreenOverlayShell.tsx:125-132 — `onKey` on Escape calls `e.stopPropagation()` and is registered `window.addEventListener("keydown", onKey, true)` (capture). primitives/PlotToolbar.tsx:312-319 — same pattern on `document` with capture for BOTH `keydown` (Escape, with `stopPropagation`) and `pointerdown`. Also window-level keydown in renderers/ImagePaneShell.tsx:881, renderers/ScatterPlot.tsx:253, media-compare/use-split-flip-keys.ts:106, stack/StackedView.tsx:75 (only use-split-flip-keys.ts:70-105 is hover/focus-gated). Failing scenario: cairn-track opens CardDetailModal, which contains a mounted plot; the user opens a pane's toolbar menu, then presses Escape intending to close the modal — PlotToolbar's capture-phase handler fires first, stops propagation, and closes only the menu; the host's modal Escape never runs. Same shape for the toolbar's document-capture `pointerdown` versus the host's SettingsPopover outside-click dismissal.
v2:314b009fe.proposal: State a keyboard/focus contract in §5: cairn-plot handlers are scoped to the mount element (focus-within or hover) and never register capture-phase document listeners that stopPropagation; add mount options `keyboard: boolean` and `portalContainer: Element` so a host can own the shortcut namespace and the stacking context. If page-level capture is genuinely required for the baked-gallery mode, gate it behind an explicit `standalone: true` mount option rather than defaulting it on for embedding hosts.

v2:2bb7601a2.claim: `Viewport.pushLayer/removeLayer` are imperative mutations of a stack that does not exist as mutable state today: the stack is a value recomputed every render from selection/stage state, so host layers are silently dropped and the "transients always sit ABOVE host layers" invariant is unimplementable as specced.
v2:2bb7601a2.evidence: The only stack constructors are pure expressions rebuilt per render: `plot-node.tsx:1038` `useViewportSettings(pushSettingsLayer([`vp-st-${paneId}`], groups?.settingsGroupId))` and `plot-selection-stage.tsx:379-382` `settingsGroupIds.reduce(pushSettingsLayer, [`vp-st-stage-${cellViewportId}`])`. `image-settings-sync.ts:145-163` states the design intent explicitly: "There is deliberately NO mutable global stack: layer lifetime stays tied to the UI scope that pushed it". Failing scenario: host calls `vp.pushLayer(L)` → stack must become `[vp-st-pane, L]`; the user then plain-clicks two panes → `PaneSelectionFrame` re-renders and evaluates line 1038, producing `[vp-st-pane, settingsGroup]`. L is gone from the stack (not below the episode layer — absent), the host's card settings vanish mid-session, and `removeLayer(L)` later has nothing to remove. There is no seam where a host layer can be spliced in, and appending on push (`pushSettingsLayer` only appends, `image-settings-sync.ts:170-175`) puts a host layer ABOVE a live episode layer, inverting the specced order.
v2:2bb7601a2.proposal: Replace the pure stack VALUE with a per-viewport ordered layer registry that owns three explicit tiers — `local < host < transient` — and make `pushLayer(layer)` an insert into the host tier (not an append). Rewrite `plot-node.tsx:1038` / `plot-selection-stage.tsx:379` to push the selection/stage layers into the *transient* tier of that registry rather than composing the stack themselves, and make `resolveSettingsStack` read the registry. Spell out in §5.4 that push order only orders layers *within* the host tier.

v2:2bb7601a2.claim: §5.4's write-routing bullet is self-contradictory: "gestures write the topmost layer … this is how card settings get persisted from gestures" cannot hold together with "while an in-page selection is active, gestures write the transient episode layer and revert on deselect". Every gesture made during a selection or enlarge episode is lost to the host, with no signal that it happened.
v2:2bb7601a2.evidence: Writes are unconditionally top-of-stack: `image-settings-sync.ts:183-190` `publishToSettingsStack` takes `stack[stack.length - 1]`, and `use-synced-image-settings.ts:92-99` is the only `set`. Transient-per-layer revert is the stated ruling (`use-synced-image-settings.ts:20-24`). Failing scenario in cairn-track: card mounts with host layer L (persisted spec) topmost; user selects two panes to compare (episode layer pushed above L), changes colormap and exposure, likes the result, deselects. The episode layer's values evaporate, the pane snaps back to L's values, `L.get()` is unchanged, `L.onChange` never fired — the user's work is silently discarded even though the spec sold host layers as the persistence path for gestures. Selection is page-global and spans React roots (`selection-store.ts:6-14`), so a user can be inside an episode at any moment a card mounts.
v2:2bb7601a2.proposal: Split write *position* from write *intent*. Give `Viewport.setSettings(patch, opts?: { layer?: SettingsLayer })` a targeted form, and let a host designate a gesture sink: `pushLayer(layer, { gestureSink: true })`, meaning gestures land in that layer even when a transient sits above it (the transient still shadows for *reads* until it drops, and the commit is applied to the sink on episode end). If that is rejected, delete the "this is how card settings get persisted from gestures" claim and give hosts an explicit `viewport.commitTo(layer)` plus an episode-end event so they can capture the value before it evaporates.

v2:2bb7601a2.claim: HOME / double-click does not clear settings — it publishes a full snapshot of the *clicked pane's* concrete defaults into the topmost layer. With a host layer topmost, one HOME pins every display key into the host's persisted state; with a host layer shared across panes, one HOME stamps one image's peak/gamma onto every other pane.
v2:2bb7601a2.evidence: `GpuImagePane.tsx:2690-2721`: `onReset` calls `publishSettings({ encoding: homeEncoding, peak: peakSeed, tonemapGamma: gammaSeed, exposureEV: 0, offset: 0, reduce: …, colorMin/colorMax…, infoPanel: undefined })` — concrete per-image seed values, explicitly "a GROUP action" (comment at 2693-2696). `plot-node.tsx:1590-1601` does the same for compare (`compareMode/diffKernel/splitPosition` written by value). `publishSettings` is the top-of-stack write. Failing scenario: a gallery card pushes one shared layer L over 8 HDR renders with different dynamic ranges; the user double-clicks render #1 to reset it; `peak: peakSeed` and `tonemapGamma: gammaSeed` of render #1 are written into L, so renders #2-8 are all re-exposed to #1's peak, and `L.get()` — the thing the host persists — now contains render #1's defaults as explicit user settings forever.
v2:2bb7601a2.proposal: Define HOME in §5.4 as a layer *clear* of the keys the pane owns in the current write-target layer (requires the unset primitive from SL-4), so the descriptor default re-emerges per pane instead of one pane's seeds being broadcast by value. Until that exists, the spec must state that HOME writes concrete values into host layers and that sharing a layer across panes with different data makes HOME non-idempotent across the group.

v2:2bb7601a2.claim: There is no way to remove a key from a layer, and `undefined` is overloaded to mean "mask the layers below" — so "persistence = serialize `layer.get()`" is not JSON-round-trippable: JSON drops the undefined-valued keys and restoring the layer changes the rendered result.
v2:2bb7601a2.evidence: Layers grow monotonically: `image-settings-sync.ts:132-143` merges with `{ ...prev, ...patch }` — nothing deletes a key. Reads are `Object.assign({}, ...layers)` (`image-settings-sync.ts:212-224`), which copies own keys *including* `undefined` ones, and the codebase relies on that: `GpuImagePane.tsx:2717-2720` comments "Explicit `undefined` CLEARS the pair in the store (flat merge), so HOME turns the bounds skin off", and `image-settings-sync.ts:80-83` documents `infoPanel: undefined` as the meaningful "back to auto" value. Failing scenario: user sets a colorRange (`colorMin/colorMax` land in the viewport-local layer), then a host layer above it takes a HOME which writes `{colorMin: undefined, colorMax: undefined}`. Host persists `JSON.stringify(layer.get())` → both keys disappear from the JSON. Next session, `createSettingsLayer(parsed)` no longer masks the layer below, the old bounds skin re-engages, and the image comes back mis-scaled. Same class of bug for `infoPanel`.
v2:2bb7601a2.proposal: Add explicit primitives — `layer.unset(keys: string[])` (real `delete` in `lastStates`, meaning "fall through to the layer below") and `layer.replace(obj)` — and make masking an explicit sentinel rather than `undefined`, or specify a serialization format that preserves present-but-undefined keys (e.g. `layer.toJSON()` emitting `{ set: {...}, masked: [...] }` and `createSettingsLayer` accepting it). §5.4's "persistence = serialize `layer.get()`" must reference that format, not raw JSON.

v2:2bb7601a2.claim: §5.2's "panes keep their settings across `update()`" silently breaks §5.5 live data: a layer value always shadows the descriptor, and HOME writes every key by value, so after one gesture or one double-click a re-authored descriptor's display settings are permanently ignored.
v2:2bb7601a2.evidence: Precedence is store-then-descriptor with no re-seeding: `plot-node.tsx:1575-1584` — `viewMode = syncMode !== undefined ? normalize(syncMode) : (override ?? descriptorMode)`; same shape for `diffKernel`/`splitPos`. Panes read the same way (`GpuImagePane.tsx:563-566`, "the one lookup: store value > prop seed"). Because HOME publishes concrete values for essentially the whole key set (`GpuImagePane.tsx:2705-2720`), after a single double-click the store holds every key. Failing scenario: a live card does `m.update(cairnPlot.image(step1200, { tonemap: "aces", colorRange: [0, 4] }))`, later `m.update(cairnPlot.image(step2400, { colorRange: [0, 40] }))` because the run's range grew. The pane keeps its layer's `colorMin/colorMax` from the earlier HOME and renders the new step blown out; the host has no API to say "this key is descriptor-authored, drop the layer override".
v2:2bb7601a2.proposal: Specify descriptor-vs-layer precedence for `update()` in §5.2: either (a) descriptor-authored settings keys that CHANGE between handles invalidate the corresponding key in the viewport-local layer (a re-seed rule, matching the existing "seed" language in the panes), or (b) document that descriptor settings are first-mount seeds only and give the host `viewport.reseedFromDescriptor(keys?)` / `layer.unset(keys)` (SL-4) to apply an authored change. Add a test in the migration gates that an `update()` with a changed `colorRange` is visible after a HOME.

v2:2bb7601a2.claim: `onSettingsChange` ("fires on any resolved-settings change (gesture, layer push/pop, sync)") and `layer.onChange` ("fires on writes INTO this layer (host or gesture)") cannot be implemented on the current bus: layer push/pop and clears emit no event at all, and the bus deliberately drops the writer's own events.
v2:2bb7601a2.evidence: Three concrete gaps in `image-settings-sync.ts`: (1) push/pop are pure value operations (`:170-180`) — no event is ever dispatched, and the React hook papers over this with a manual `bump()` in an effect keyed on the stack string (`use-synced-image-settings.ts:83-90`), machinery a non-React `Viewport` object does not have; (2) `clearImageSettings` (`:238-241`) deletes the snapshot and bumps the version but dispatches nothing, so every subscriber's resolved settings change with no notification (today it is only survivable because `useSeedGroupOnFormation` (`use-synced-image-settings.ts:122-127`) immediately publishes after it); (3) `subscribeImageSettings` ignores events whose `sourceId` matches the subscriber (`:264-267`), so a layer that writes with its own source id never observes its own `set` — contradicting "host or gesture". Failing scenario: host persists on `onSettingsChange`. User selects two panes, drags exposure (episode layer write → event fires → host persists exposure 3.0), then deselects. Resolved settings revert to 0.0 with NO event; the host's stored value stays 3.0 and diverges from what is on screen until the next unrelated write.
v2:2bb7601a2.proposal: Make stack composition an evented operation: dispatch on attach/detach/clear (a `layers-changed` event carrying the viewport's new resolved value), and drop the echo filter for handle-based subscribers (keep `sourceId` filtering only for the pane-to-pane mirror path). v2:4818747bb.claim: `MountedPlot.viewports` / `MountedPlot.viewport` cannot be populated when `mount()` returns, and can never enumerate off-screen panes: rendering is an async concurrent-root render, and every leaf is behind a viewport-lazy `IntersectionObserver` gate.
