` with no canvas until its IntersectionObserver fires. pool.ts:129/575-581 caps live panes at 12 with eviction on activation. Failing scenario: a 30-card dashboard, user calls `m.screenshot()`. Panes below the fold are placeholders → their regions composite blank (or the call throws at plot-to-png.ts:217). For the mounted ones, `screenshot()` returns a Promise, so any `await` between a pane's repaint and its `drawImage` voids the same-task guarantee above; and driving all 30 repaints first, then compositing, means panes 1-18 were parked by `evictOverCap` during the pass and their next `activateEntry` resets `canvas.width` (pool.ts:615-616), clearing them.
v2:122677e8b.proposal: §5.2 must specify screenshot as a two-phase, per-pane protocol: (1) an explicit `hydrate()`/eager step that mounts every gated pane and awaits readiness, returning a diagnostic list of panes that could not be made live; (2) per pane, a synchronous `repaint → drawImage` performed under a single rAF, with the pool given a temporary "pin" so a pane already captured is not evicted mid-pass. Also state the >cap behavior explicitly (capture in cap-sized batches, re-rendering each batch). §9.5 should be closed before M0 lands screenshot, not after — the readback timing is a shape constraint on the API, not a detail.

v2:122677e8b.claim: §5.2's `viewports: readonly Viewport[]` — "All viewports (descriptor-tree order). Stable identity across update()" — cannot be satisfied without defeating viewport-lazy mounting, because settings today live in per-pane React state plus a per-group EventTarget bus, not in a mount-independent, path-keyed store.
v2:122677e8b.evidence: plot-node.tsx:1398-1412 — LazyGate exists precisely because "a leaf/compare pane is expensive to mount: images decode, WebGPU pipelines compile, 3D scenes build, addons eval", and the real child mounts only when the IntersectionObserver fires (:1469-1478); the only escapes are `?eager=1` / `window.__cairnPlotEagerMount` (:1414-1419). image-settings-sync.ts:1-32 — the settings system is "one `EventTarget` per `groupId`" where "each viewport owns ONE concrete settings set" held by the pane; there is no registry keyed by descriptor path. Failing scenario: a host mounts a 30-card grid and, on `onReady`, iterates `m.viewports` to `pushLayer` a persisted card layer onto each (the exact §5.6 `layers` flow). Either the array only contains the ~4 panes currently near the viewport — violating "All viewports" and "stable identity across update()", and the other 26 silently never receive the layer — or the implementation forces eager mount, which compiles 30 WebGPU pipelines and decodes 30 sources at once and instantly exceeds `MAX_LIVE_SWAPCHAINS` (pool.ts:129).
v2:122677e8b.proposal: Define `Viewport` as a HANDLE addressed by tree path that exists whether or not the pane is mounted, backed by a new path-keyed settings store that the pane reads on mount (so `pushLayer`/`setSettings` before mount is legal and applies on first paint). Say so explicitly in §5.3 and answer §9.2 the same way: a path that disappears leaves a detached handle whose writes are retained and re-applied if the path returns. Add a stated invariant to §5.2: enumerating `viewports` MUST NOT force a mount.

v2:122677e8b.claim: The one shared GPUDevice is memoized forever with no loss-recovery path, so a single device loss on a long-lived live dashboard (§3 goal 3) permanently degrades every pane on the page to the CPU fallback — and §4 exposes no way for the host to recover.
v2:122677e8b.evidence: device.ts:43,60-65 — `sharedDevicePromise` is memoized on first call and only ever cleared by `resetSharedDevice()` (:73-81), which the module doc marks "(for tests)" and which does not appear in §4's public surface. webgpu/device.ts:667-690 attaches exactly one `gpuDevice.lost.then` watcher whose entire job is bookkeeping — it sets `lostRef.info` for readback error enrichment and calls `recordContextLossEvent` (test-only instrumentation); it does NOT clear the memo or notify panes. Failing scenario: an 8-hour training run with a live dashboard open; VRAM pressure from PERF-3/PERF-4 (or a driver reset / GPU-process crash / laptop GPU switch) loses the device. From then on every `activateEntry` throws, `attemptRender` catches and warns (pool.ts:748-757), and every image/compare pane on the page falls back to the legacy CPU pane — forever, because `getSharedDevice()` keeps handing back the same dead device. The user's only fix is a full page reload, which also discards all settings layers.
v2:122677e8b.proposal: §4/§5 must include a device lifecycle: on `lost`, invalidate the memo, park+dispose every pool entry, drop the diff cache, and emit a host-observable event (e.g. `MountedPlot.onDeviceLost`) so panes can re-acquire on the next render. Add `resetSharedDevice`-equivalent recovery to the public entry (not just tests) and a harness case using the existing `?forceEngineFail` hook (pool.ts:594-598) that proves a pane recovers to GPU rendering after a simulated loss.

v2:122677e8b.claim: The per-pane park/restore IntersectionObserver has zero hysteresis (`threshold: 0`, no rootMargin) while park destroys the ENTIRE retained-texture set, so ordinary scrolling and resizes at the fold cause repeated full teardown/re-upload cycles — the opposite of LazyGate's deliberately generous margin.
v2:122677e8b.evidence: GpuImagePane.tsx:1157-1178 — `new IntersectionObserver(…, { threshold: 0 })` with no `rootMargin`; on `!isIntersecting` it calls `handle.park()` immediately, on re-intersect `handle.restore()` plus a forced re-render tick. pool.ts:544-564 `parkEntry` → `clearRetained` (pool.ts:538-541) destroys every retained texture, and `activateEntry` (pool.ts:610-636) re-`createSurface`s and re-uploads both slots. Compare plot-node.tsx:1403-1405/1476, where the MOUNT gate deliberately uses a "generous rootMargin" (`LAZY_ROOT_MARGIN`). Failing scenario: a pane sitting at the fold of a 30-card dashboard during a momentum scroll or a window resize crosses the 0-threshold boundary several times in under a second; each crossing destroys up to 7 textures (bound + 6 retained) and re-uploads the full source on the way back, and each restore may also evict another pane via `evictOverCap`.
v2:122677e8b.proposal: Give the park observer a rootMargin (e.g. one viewport height) and debounce park by a few hundred ms so a boundary oscillation is free; keep `setVisible` immediate so the LRU's off-screen preference still updates instantly. Optionally decouple park from retention: park should free the surface and bound textures but may keep the retained LRU under the byte budget from PERF-4. Fold this into the §5 mounting contract so hosts can rely on stated hysteresis rather than pane-internal defaults.

v2:3953f0c82.claim: §5.5 Tier-1 live data ("fetch, author a new handle, call m.update(h2)") leaks every payload forever and cannot hit the "unchanged content = no re-decode/re-upload" promise, because runtime hashes are random-per-call and the runtime store has no delete path.
v2:3953f0c82.evidence: `mintRuntimeHash()` is a counter + `Math.random()` — NOT content-derived (ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/viewport/runtime-store.ts:122-126); every `cairnPlot.image(f32, …)` mints a fresh hash (builder/data.ts:103-107, 213-217). Mounting registers entries into a page-global `window.__cairnPlotRuntimeStore` Map (runtime-store.ts:61-64, 74-85) via plot-bootstrap.tsx:94-96. There is no `delete`/evict/refcount anywhere in runtime-store.ts, and `unmount` only tears down the React root (plot-bootstrap.tsx:103, builder/handle.ts:86-88). Failing scenario: a 1 Hz live 1024×1024 f32 RGB card calls `m.update(h2)` each tick → 12 MB/s of Float32Array retained in a global Map that nothing ever prunes; after 10 minutes the tab is at ~7 GB. Same run also re-decodes/re-uploads every tick even when the bytes are byte-identical, because the resolve key is the fresh random hash — directly contradicting §5.5 ("unchanged content = no re-decode/re-upload; scrubbing warm steps is instant") and §5.2's hold discipline.
v2:3953f0c82.proposal: (a) Content-address runtime entries: hash the bytes, or accept an author-supplied `key`/`dataKey` in the builder opts, so re-authoring identical data reuses the entry and the resolve cache actually hits. (b) Give `MountedPlot` ownership of the runtime entries it registered: refcount per hash, release on `update()` (entries no longer referenced by the new descriptor) and on `unmount()`. (c) State the ownership/lifetime contract explicitly in §5.2 and §5.5 — right now the spec assumes a cache that the builder's hashing defeats.

v2:3953f0c82.claim: §5.4's promised stack order `[viewport-local, ...host layers, ...in-page transients]` is not constructible in the existing model, and the enlarge/compare stage builds a stack that DROPS host layers entirely — so a host layer's settings silently vanish the moment the user enlarges.
v2:3953f0c82.evidence: A pane's stack is built at render from context with room for exactly ONE group id: `useViewportSettings(pushSettingsLayer([`vp-st-${paneId}`], groups?.settingsGroupId))` (ui/src/plot-node.tsx:1037-1038). The stage cell does NOT extend the origin pane's stack — it builds a brand-new one: `settingsGroupIds.reduce(pushSettingsLayer, ['vp-st-stage-'+cellViewportId])` where `settingsGroupIds = [selection-episode, stage-open]` (ui/src/plot-selection-stage.tsx:378-383, 515-521). Host layers pushed onto the origin viewport appear in neither list. The internal design explicitly rejects the mutable stack §5.4 requires: "There is deliberately NO mutable global stack: layer lifetime stays tied to the UI scope that pushed it, so pops can never be unbalanced or forgotten" (viewport/image-settings-sync.ts:151-157) and "Pushes are PURE (new stack values) — layer lifetime is the pushing scope's lifetime" (renderers/use-synced-image-settings.ts:23-26). Failing scenario: host pushes layer L={exposureEV:+2} onto two viewports; both render at +2. User selects both panes and clicks Enlarge → StageCell's stack is `[vp-st-stage-N, sel-episode, stage-N]`, L is absent → the enlarged panes render at exposure 0. Close the stage → +2 is back. §5.4 promises the opposite ordering (transients ABOVE host layers).
v2:3953f0c82.proposal: Make host layers part of the stack the panes construct, not an imperative side-channel: thread them through a `HostSettingsLayersContext` that BOTH `PaneSelectionFrame` (plot-node.tsx:1037) and `StageCell` (plot-selection-stage.tsx:378) consume, and spec the stage stack as `originStack ++ [episode, stageOpen]`. Then drop `Viewport.pushLayer/removeLayer` in favour of the declarative `<Plot layers={…}>` prop (mount option for non-React hosts) — an imperative push/remove against a value recomputed each render is unimplementable without reintroducing exactly the mutable stack the internal design forbids.

v2:3953f0c82.claim: §5.3 `setSettings` writing "as a user gesture would: into the TOPMOST layer" corrupts host state: a host write lands in a transient layer it does not own and evaporates when that layer drops.
v2:3953f0c82.evidence: Writes go to the top of the stack unconditionally: `publishToSettingsStack` takes `stack[stack.length-1]` (viewport/image-settings-sync.ts:183-190), and the top is the selection episode while ≥2 panes are selected (plot-node.tsx:1027, 1037-1038) or the per-open stage layer while the stage is up (plot-selection-stage.tsx:514-521). Layers are transient by design: "dropping a layer (unselect, stage close) reverts every viewport below it — values changed while the layer was on top evaporate with it" (use-synced-image-settings.ts:18-22). Failing scenario: the card restores persisted settings on mount with `vp.setSettings({exposureEV: 2})`; the user happens to have that pane in a 2-pane selection → the write lands in `cp-sel-st-<episode>`; the user deselects → the restored value evaporates and `onSettingsChange` reports exposure 0, which the host then persists as the user's setting. Compounding: the viewport-local layer `vp-st-${paneId}` is not addressable from the API at all, so §5.4's "persistence = serialize layer.get()" cannot capture any setting the user changed with no host layer on top.
v2:3953f0c82.proposal: Answer open question 7 as NOT-topmost: `setSettings` writes a dedicated per-viewport host layer that sits directly above viewport-local and below all transients, so a host write is durable and never contaminated by a selection episode. Keep gesture writes routing to topmost. Separately expose the viewport-local layer for read/restore (e.g. `Viewport.localLayer: SettingsLayer`), otherwise the settings boundary cannot round-trip the default case.

v2:3953f0c82.claim: `Viewport.id` ("the descriptor tree path") is not the identity settings are keyed on, so §5.2's "panes … keep their settings" is only true by accident of React instance survival — and every remount orphans a settings layer in a global map that is never pruned.
v2:3953f0c82.evidence: Settings are keyed on a module-counter pane id, not the path: `const [paneId] = useState(nextSelectionPaneId)` (ui/src/plot-node.tsx:937) feeding `vp-st-${paneId}` (plot-node.tsx:1038). The layer stores live in a `globalThis`-anchored registry (`__cairnPlotImageSettingsBus__`, image-settings-sync.ts:107-118) whose entries are removed only by `clearImageSettings` (line 238, used solely for selection-group formation) or the test reset (line 249). The merge cache is keyed by `stack.join(" ")` with no eviction despite the comment claiming boundedness (image-settings-sync.ts:207, 213-223). Failing scenario: §5.2 says "A leaf whose renderer changes at a path is a remount at that path only" — that remount mints a new `paneId`, so viewport-local settings silently reset to defaults while the old `vp-st-N` entry (and its stack's mergeCache entry) stays resident forever. In a long-lived tracker SPA where cards mount/unmount on every navigation, `lastStates` + `layerVersions` + `mergeCache` grow monotonically for the session.
v2:3953f0c82.proposal: Derive the viewport-local layer id from the stable identity §5.3 already promises (mount id + descriptor path), so settings survive a same-path remount and are addressable/restorable. Add explicit layer disposal (`SettingsLayer.dispose()`, plus automatic disposal of `vp-st-*` on final viewport teardown) that deletes from `lastStates`/`layerVersions` and invalidates matching `mergeCache` keys. Spec what `Viewport.id` means when a path disappears across `update()` (open question 2) — today the object would silently address nothing.

v2:3953f0c82.claim: §5.6's one-line "StrictMode-safe" hides two concrete failures: the library force-wraps host content in `React.StrictMode` with no opt-out, and `mount()` calls `createRoot` unguarded on the target element.
v2:3953f0c82.evidence: Every mount path hard-codes StrictMode: `root.render(<React.StrictMode><PlotApp …/></React.StrictMode>)` at plot-bootstrap.tsx:97-102, and again at 258-262 and 297-302. A host that deliberately runs without StrictMode (common when GPU init is expensive) cannot turn it off inside a nested root, so in dev every pane double-runs its acquire effect — two `getSharedDevice()` awaits and an `acquirePane`/`releasePane` churn per pane (renderers/GpuImagePane.tsx:1103-1112, 1130-1137) against a page-global 12-slot LRU (engine/pool.ts:129, 576). Second failure: `mount()` resolves the element and calls `ReactDOM.createRoot(el)` with no guard (handle.ts:84-88 → plot-bootstrap.tsx:97). Under HOST StrictMode, `<Plot>`'s mount effect runs mount→cleanup→mount on the SAME element: if the adapter's guard skips the cleanup unmount, the second `createRoot(el)` throws React's "You are calling ReactDOMClient.createRoot() on a container that has already been passed to createRoot() before"; if it does unmount, `root.unmount()` invoked from inside the host's effect cleanup is deferred when React is mid-render (unmount flushes via flushSync, which warns and schedules instead), so the deferred null-render can clear the container AFTER the second root painted → permanently blank pane. Neither case is covered by "idempotent mount/unmount; effects guard double-invoke".
v2:3953f0c82.proposal: (a) Remove the internal `React.StrictMode` wrapper from the host-facing mount path (keep it, if wanted, behind a `mount(el, {strict: true})` opt-in used by the standalone entries only). (b) Make mounting idempotent per element: keep a `WeakMap<Element, Root>` and call `root.render()` on an existing root instead of `createRoot`. (c) Spec `MountedPlot.unmount()` as idempotent and safe to call during a host effect cleanup (defer to a microtask, and make a subsequent `mount()` on the same element cancel a pending unmount). (d) Add a gate: an adapter test that mounts/unmounts/remounts `<Plot>` inside `<React.StrictMode>` and asserts one root, one pane handle, no console error.

v2:3953f0c82.claim: Embedding installs page-global UI and document-level listeners that `MountedPlot.unmount()` cannot undo and the host cannot scope, disable, or z-order — a hard blocker for plots inside host modals/drawers.
v2:3953f0c82.evidence: `ensureSelectionOverlayHost()` appends a div to `document.body` and creates a THIRD React root, guarded by a module singleton with no teardown outside tests (ui/src/plot-selection-stage.tsx:936-952, 955-964); it is called from every `PlotApp` mount effect (plot-bootstrap.tsx:181-183). That root installs document-level CAPTURE `pointerdown`/`pointerup` listeners for the page's lifetime — unconditionally, not gated on a non-empty selection — which call `store.clear()` on any click not matching a hard-coded selector whitelist (plot-selection-stage.tsx:848-881). The action bar portals to `document.body` at `zIndex: 2147482000` (line 780, 822-824) and the stage uses the shared fullscreen overlay shell. The selection store is a document-scoped singleton (`getGlobalSelectionStore`, line 495, 832), so panes belonging to two unrelated host cards join ONE selection and the action bar appears over the host's chrome. Failing scenario: cairn-track opens a host modal containing a `<Plot>`; the user shift-clicks two panes and hits Enlarge → the stage renders above the host modal at z-index 2^31-ish; closing every plot and unmounting the card leaves the body node plus both capture listeners intercepting the host app's clicks for the rest of the session.
v2:3953f0c82.proposal: Add mount/`<Plot>` options the spec currently lacks: `selection: "off" | "scoped" | "page"` (default `"scoped"` for embedded hosts), `portalContainer?: Element`, and `zIndexBase?: number`. Refcount `ensureSelectionOverlayHost` so the last `unmount()` tears the host down, and attach the document capture listeners only while a selection is non-empty. Until this exists, §5.2's `unmount()` should not be described as teardown.

v2:3953f0c82.claim: §5.6's "one React copy when the host bundles cairn-plot source" is asserted but not enforced: the ESM `cairnPlot` export deliberately resolves the mounter from a first-wins window global, so a host page that also carries any inline core bundle renders host-authored handles through a different React copy.
v2:3953f0c82.evidence: The default export is UNBOUND by design — "the default `cairnPlot` export leaves the mounter unbound, so `.mount()`/`.toElement()` resolve `window.__cairnPlotMountObject` on demand" (builder/index.ts module doc; `export const cairnPlot = createCairnPlot();` with no mounter), and `resolveMounter` reads `globalThis.__cairnPlotMountObject` whenever no explicit mounter was bound (handle.ts:49-58). Installation is first-wins with an early return: `if (window.__cairnPlotMountObject) return;` (plot-bootstrap.tsx:112-115); the same first-wins pattern guards `__cairnPlotBootstrap`, `__cairnPlotRegisterRenderer`, `__cairnPlotHasRenderer` (lines 272-283). The codebase already treats cross-bundle duplication as a live hazard — the settings bus had to be moved onto `globalThis` precisely because two bundle copies of the module were two disjoint registries (image-settings-sync.ts:93-118), while the merge cache stayed module-local per bundle (line 204-207). Failing scenario: cairn-track (source-compiled via the vite alias, per §4/§5.6) renders a page that also embeds a Python-emitted report's `core.iife.js` inline (§2 lists notebook/inline as a supported shape). The IIFE installs the globals first; the host's `cairnPlot.image(...).mount(el)` from §5.1 then renders through the IIFE's React + its registry, host context is a different copy, and the host's `Viewport`/layer objects address a mergeCache the rendering bundle never consults.
v2:3953f0c82.proposal: The `cairn-plot`/`cairn-plot/react` entries must bind their OWN mounter at module scope (`createCairnPlot(mountDescriptorObject)`) and never fall through to `globalThis`. Stamp the window globals with a build/instance id and log a loud, actionable warning when a second instance is detected. Spec the multi-instance rule explicitly in §5.6 rather than asserting single-copy.

v2:3953f0c82.claim: §5.6's `onSettingsChange` has no defined firing phase, no coalescing, and an echo-guard mismatch — as specced it will either miss writes or feed back into itself, and at best fires at pointermove rate into host React state.
v2:3953f0c82.evidence: Resolved settings are read DURING RENDER (`return { settings: resolveSettingsStack(stack), set }`, renderers/use-synced-image-settings.ts:103), and the re-render signal is a bus subscription (lines 83-90). Publishes are synchronous `dispatchEvent` with no batching (viewport/image-settings-sync.ts:132-143) driven from live gestures (exposure/gamma sliders, split-divider drags — the key list at lines 41-84). So the natural implementation ("call the host back where the new value is computed") invokes `onSettingsChange` inside cairn-plot's render pass; a host that calls `setState` there gets React's "Cannot update a component while rendering a different component". Echo mismatch: `subscribeImageSettings` silently drops events whose `sourceId` matches the subscriber's (lines 264-267), and each viewport's `set` publishes under its own per-hook sourceId (use-synced-image-settings.ts:73-74, 94). A host subscription reusing the viewport's sourceId misses every gesture from that viewport; a host subscription with its own sourceId means §5.4's `layer.onChange` ("fires on writes INTO this layer (host or gesture)") re-enters on the host's own `layer.set()` — a host mirroring settings into React state loops.
v2:3953f0c82.proposal: Spec it: `onSettingsChange` fires from a passive effect / microtask, never during render; coalesce to at most one callback per animation frame per viewport with latest-wins (this answers open question 4 — the write path has zero coalescing today, so it must be added at the adapter). Define `layer.onChange` as NOT firing for the caller's own `layer.set()` (or add an `{ echo: boolean }` option), and give the host subscription a distinct sourceId so it observes gestures from every attached viewport.

v2:e69680e07.claim: §8's "additive keys" rule is false for the descriptor: the existing descriptor contract is closed (`additionalProperties:false` in the committed JSON schema, `extra="forbid"` on every pydantic model), so an old reader HARD-REJECTS a new descriptor instead of ignoring the new key. There is also no version field anywhere to detect the mismatch, and §5.5 Tier-2 silently requires a new DataSpec branch that must land in three repos-worth of files at once.
v2:e69680e07.evidence: `schema/cairn-plot-spec.schema.json:28` (`PlotDescriptor.additionalProperties:false`, repeated at :68, :92, :153); `src/cairn_plot/spec.py:42-46` (`class _Strict(BaseModel): model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")`) — every DataSpec/node model inherits it; `tests/test_spec_conformance.py:40-47` enumerates the five DataSpec branches by `kind` const and fails on any added branch. `grep -rn 'schemaVersion|schema_version|descriptorVersion' ui/src src` → zero hits: the descriptor carries no version (`ui/src/plot-descriptor.ts:235-246` — only `root`/`mode`/`endpoint`). Failing scenario: spec §5.5 line 200 shows `cairnPlot.line({ src: "track://run/17/loss" })`. Today that string can only ride in `DataSpec{kind:"url"}.src`, which `resolveDataProps` feeds to `resolveFinalUrl(data.src)` (`plot-descriptor.ts:368-371`) — a `fetch("track://…")` that throws. So Tier-2 must add a new `kind`. Emit that descriptor and hand it to a cairn install whose `cairn_plot` wheel predates the change: `PlotDescriptorSpec.model_validate` raises ValidationError on the unknown `kind` rather than degrading, and pyproject.toml:21 declares `"cairn-plot"` with no version bound so that pairing is installable today.
v2:e69680e07.proposal: Add `schema: 1` (integer) to `PlotDescriptor` NOW, before any host writes descriptors, and state the reader rule in §8: unknown `schema` > mine → refuse with a named error; unknown DataSpec `kind`/node `kind` at an equal-or-lower schema → render a typed placeholder leaf, never throw. Relax `additionalProperties` to `true` on `PlotDescriptor`/`PlotLeafNode` (keep it false on the leaf DataSpec branches) and drop `extra="forbid"` to `extra="ignore"` on the node models, or §8's "additive keys" sentence must be replaced with "the descriptor is a closed schema; every addition is a lockstep TS+schema+pydantic change and breaks older readers." Also spell out in §5.5 that Tier-2 adds a DataSpec branch and how it composes with the root-level `mode`/`endpoint` that today binds the WHOLE tree to one DataSource (`plot-descriptor.ts:238-246`).

v2:e69680e07.claim: §5.3's `ViewportSettings` = "the SAME shapes the settings stores hold internally" is unimplementable as written for `kind:"image"`: there are TWO live image-settings vocabularies with colliding key names and incompatible value domains, and the spec never says which one becomes the wire contract.
v2:e69680e07.evidence: `ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/viewport/image-settings-sync.ts:41-84` (`ImageSyncSettings`: `exposureEV`, `offset`, `colorMin`/`colorMax`, `encoding`, `compareMode?: string` documented at :68-70 as `"split" | "diff"`, `splitPosition`, `diffKernel`). `ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/media-compare/compare-settings.ts:40-100` (`MediaCompareSettings`: `exposure`, `offset`, `gamma`, `brightness`, `contrast`, `zoom`, `pan`, `mode: MediaCompareModeKind`, `compareMode?: "side-by-side"|"split"|"blend"`, `splitPosition`, `colormap: Colormap`, `diffMode`). `compareMode` is the same key with two disjoint enums; `offset` and `splitPosition` are the same key in two structures; `exposure` vs `exposureEV` are two names that may or may not be the same quantity. Failing scenario: cairn-track's cards persist the `MediaCompareSettings`-shaped blob under `version: 1` (`cairn/ui/src/lib/card-settings.ts:79-83, 116-161`), and §5.4 line 186 tells the host to persist `layer.get()` — an `ImageSyncSettings` blob — the same way. Both land in the same per-card record; a card whose old blob has `compareMode: "side-by-side"` and whose new layer writes `compareMode: "diff"` now has one key meaning two things, with `migrateLegacyMode` (`media-compare/migrate-legacy-mode.ts:63-70`) keying off exactly that field.
v2:e69680e07.proposal: Pick ONE and say so in §5.3 with a table: `ViewportSettings['image']` is `ImageSyncSettings`, `MediaCompareSettings` becomes private card state (or vice versa). If both must survive the migration window, rename the colliding keys on the public side (`compareView`, `exposureEV`, `splitPos`) and ship a `migrateViewportSettings(kind, blob)` in the `cairn-plot` entry that consumes the `MediaCompareSettings` shape — §4 already promises "settings types + migrations" but nothing in §5 or §7 says what the migration migrates FROM.

v2:e69680e07.claim: "persistence = serialize `layer.get()`" (§5.4) is lossy today: `undefined`-as-a-present-value is load-bearing in the settings model, and it does not survive JSON or the YAML report round-trip that cairn-track actually uses.

v2:bdf99058a.claim: `ViewportSettings` as specced (a discriminated union by kind, "the SAME shapes the settings stores hold internally", §5.3) does not exist and has no analogue for any non-image kind. Chart state is React `useState` inside the standalone adapter; 3D state is an app-supplied generic. M1 therefore starts with the card that has *zero* store backing, not the cheapest one.
v2:bdf99058a.evidence: `ViewportSettings` today is `{ settings: ImageSyncSettings | null; set }` — image-only, not a union (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/renderers/use-synced-image-settings.ts:51-61). Its vocabulary is encoding/tonemap/peak/exposureEV/offset/compareMode/diffKernel/channelSelect (viewport/image-settings-sync.ts:36-88) — nothing for xScale/yScale/smoothing/lineType/legend/tooltip. The scalar leaf keeps `viewport` and `promotedSeries` in local `useState` in the standalone adapter, seeded from descriptor props and never published anywhere (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/plot-renderers.tsx:170-193). 3D settings are a *host-provided* generic `TSettings` (`ViewportPaneProps<MeshViewportItem, MeshViewState, MeshViewportSettings>`, viewport/mesh-viewport.tsx:88-104, :347) — MeshVisualCard owns them in card settings; they never touch the layer stack. So for ScalarPlotCard (M1) every one of its 12 settings keys (ScalarPlotCard.tsx:48-67) needs a new store + a new union arm before `getSettings/setSettings/pushLayer` mean anything.
v2:bdf99058a.proposal: Make the union real and explicit in the spec: `type ViewportSettings = ImageViewportSettings | ChartViewportSettings | Mesh… | …`, each with a `kind` tag, and add a §5.x table mapping every existing per-kind settings type to its arm plus which ones must be *built* (chart: all of them; mesh/pointcloud/volume/boxes: promote the app-supplied `*ViewportSettings` into cairn-plot-owned stores). Re-order §7: M1 should be an image card (already store-backed, already layer-aware) and the chart-settings store should be its own milestone with the scalar card behind it.

v2:bdf99058a.claim: There is no runtime capability/option-enumeration API, so no card can build its settings UI. §6's re-entry story ("options/enumerations render in pane toolbars") contradicts how every real card works: cairn-track hides the pane toolbar and drives everything from its own menus, using imported enumerations and *window globals* to know what is available.
v2:bdf99058a.evidence: cairn-track explicitly runs panes with the toolbar hidden and drives display settings as controlled props: "With the cairn-plot pane toolbar hidden (`toolbar={false}`), cairn's own settings menu drives these" (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn/cairn/ui/src/components/card-kit/visual-compare-settings.ts:20-23). The menus are built from lib enumerations imported into app code: `COLORMAP_OPTIONS`/`DIVERGING_COLORMAPS`/`enumerateCompareModeOptions`/`canCrossTypeCompare` (VisualContentCard.tsx:26-38, :1078-1092), and `LIB_COLORMAP_OPTIONS.map(o => ({value:o.id,label:o.label}))` in TensorCard.tsx:14,64-65 and HistogramCard.tsx:17,59-60. Worse, the diff-kernel list is *asynchronously GPU-gated* and reaches the app only through `window.__cairnPlotDiffMenuModes` + the `cairn-plot:gpu-image-ready` event (VisualContentCard.tsx:117-135). Option availability is also data-dependent: HistogramCard hides "heatmap" below 4 steps (HistogramCard.tsx:127,238-248); TensorCard hides the colormap select unless heatmap and generates one slice slider per leading dim of the resolved array (TensorCard.tsx:188,350-373). None of that is derivable from `ViewportSettings` TS types alone.
v2:bdf99058a.proposal: Add a fourth pillar next to descriptor/settings/screenshot/data-sources: a settings SCHEMA surface. `viewport.describeSettings(): SettingsField[]` where each field carries `{key, type, options:[{id,label,disabled,reason}], min/max/step, available:boolean}`, recomputed from the pane's *current* resolved content and device capabilities, plus `viewport.onDescribeChange(cb)` so the GPU-ready and content-resolved transitions push. Kill `window.__cairnPlot*` as the capability channel in the same change.

v2:bdf99058a.claim: M3 ("migrate the 3D cards — descriptor leaves replace the viewport-kit composition") is unimplementable against the current builder: `cairnPlot.mesh/pointcloud/volume/boxes` throw unconditionally from JS. §2 lists them as existing surface, which is misleading.

v2:bdf99058a.claim: `update()`'s positional-by-tree-path correspondence (§5.2) silently moves per-pane settings onto the wrong content, because every multi-series card keeps its panes in *sorted* order — adding one series shifts every pane after the insertion point.
v2:bdf99058a.evidence: Metric lists are canonically sorted: `unique.sort((a,b) => seriesKey(a).localeCompare(seriesKey(b)))` (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn/cairn/ui/src/components/card-kit/use-card-series.ts:109, doc :27,40) and ScalarPlotCard re-sorts on every metrics patch (ScalarPlotCard.tsx:143-149). VisualContentCard renders one pane per metric in that order and indexes per-pane reference baselines positionally (`perPaneHash(pi)`, VisualContentCard.tsx:668,989). Failing scenario: a 3-pane image card with metrics `[b_loss, c_loss, d_loss]`; the user has zoomed pane `root.1` (c_loss) and pinned a per-pane REF on it. Drag in `a_render`; the sorted list becomes `[a_render, b_loss, c_loss, d_loss]`; path `root.1` now holds `b_loss`. Per §5.2 the renderer is unchanged at that path, so the pane is kept and c_loss's zoom + colormap + REF apply to b_loss, while a_render (path `root.0`) inherits b_loss's state. No error, no remount, silently wrong — and the same shift corrupts the persisted card settings on the next write.
v2:bdf99058a.proposal: Make identity author-supplied and required for containers: `cairnPlot.grid(children, {keys: string[]})` or a `key` opt on every builder, lowered onto the descriptor node; `update()` matches by `key` first, path only as a fallback for keyless nodes. Resolve open question 1 as "keys, not positions", and answer open question 2 by spec'ing that a `Viewport` whose key disappears becomes `detached` (id retained, `getSettings()` throws or returns last-known, `onSettingsChange` unsubscribed) rather than being re-pointed.

v2:bdf99058a.claim: The Viewport has no interaction/event channel, only settings. Several cards route *pane interactions* into app-global state that is not a setting; those wires have no home in the API and cannot be re-created from descriptors (functions are not JSON) or from `onSettingsChange`.
v2:bdf99058a.evidence: ScalarPlot exposes `onSeriesClick` and `selectedSeriesKeys` (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/renderers/ScalarPlot.tsx:52-53,259,384-385,395-398); ScalarPlotCard wires the click to the app-wide run selection (`onSeriesClick: (key) => toggle(seriesKeyToRunId.get(key))`, ScalarPlotCard.tsx:551-555) which is shared across *other cards* via `useRunSelection`. The standalone descriptor path can never carry these: `plot-renderers.tsx:177-192` spreads only JSON descriptor props into `ScalarPlot`, so `onSeriesClick`/`onNaturalSize` are structurally unreachable through §5.1.
v2:bdf99058a.proposal: Add an events surface to §5.3: `viewport.on(event, cb): () => void` with a small closed vocabulary — `"pick"` (series key / pixel / primitive id), `"dragstart"` (payload identifying the leaf, so the host can attach its own DataTransfer), `"contentsize"` (natural size + aspect), `"regionselect"` — and the mirrored *inputs* (`highlight`/`selection` as a settings key, e.g. `selectedKeys: string[]`, so the app can push its cross-card selection down). v2:bdf99058a.claim: Hosts can read settings but never *derived* state or derived data, so the card chrome that lives outside the pane (colorbar, subtitle, CSV/composite export) breaks. `screenshot()` is also far narrower than what the cards actually export.
v2:bdf99058a.evidence: (a) The colorbar is card-level, computed outside every pane from resolved items: `viewport.activeColorbar({items, referenceItems, settings, mode, nativeMode})` → `colorRange` which is then pushed *back down* into the pane as a controlled prop (VisualContentCard.tsx:851-859,:966), and rendered in card chrome (`<Colorbar …/>` :1453,:1462). §6 makes `Colorbar` and colormap LUTs private with no replacement for the derived min/max. (b) `getSettings()` cannot help: the stack resolves to `ImageSyncSettings | null` — the *sparse override* set, `null` when no layer has been written (use-synced-image-settings.ts:51-58, image-settings-sync.ts:212-224), so a freshly mounted pane reports no tonemap/encoding at all even though one is effectively active. (c) Export: ScalarPlotCard's CSV writes the *transformed* series (`emaSmooth`/`filterOutliers` output, ScalarPlotCard.tsx:190-201,567-575) — if those transforms become settings inside the pane per §6, the host loses the data it exports. Its PNG rasterizes the whole card DOM (`exportChartPng(cardRef.current)`, :577 → `plotToPng`, lib/download.ts:79-86), not a pane. VisualContentCard's export is a labeled composite assembled from artifact URLs with REF pairing, `skipColormap` per pane and an appended colorbar strip built from `getColormapLUT` + `DIVERGING_COLORMAPS` (VisualContentCard.tsx:977-1012) — none of it reachable from `MountedPlot.screenshot()`.
v2:bdf99058a.proposal: Add (1) `viewport.getInfo(): { effectiveSettings, colorRange, colormap, naturalSize, channels, dataStats }` + `onInfoChange`, so out-of-pane chrome is driven by resolved state instead of by the override layer; (2) `viewport.getData(): DataPayload` (post-transform) so CSV/table export survives moving transforms behind settings; (3) a fourth *pure* entry point `cairn-plot/data` exporting the framework-free helpers the host legitimately needs — `computeTableDiff` (TableCard.tsx:35,336-337), `checkFigureMergeable`/`mergeFigures` (FigureInteractiveCard.tsx:20-21,374,384), `parseNpy`/`parseNpz`, `getColormapLUT`, `emaSmooth`/`filterOutliers`/`strideDownsample` — rather than pretending descriptors can express "tell me if these figures are mergeable so I can enable a menu item".

v2:bdf99058a.claim: The public layer/settings API drops the echo guard the internal bus relies on, so the obvious React host wiring (persist on change, re-apply on prop change) is a feedback loop with no documented escape.
v2:bdf99058a.evidence: The internal bus is explicitly echo-guarded: "each publish carries the publisher's `sourceId`; a subscriber ignores events whose `sourceId` matches its own" and callers must "publish only from genuine local control changes … never from an effect watching the override state itself" (/Users/doeringc/workspace/cairn-plot/ui/src/lib/cairn-plot/viewport/image-settings-sync.ts:22-31; source ids minted per pane in use-synced-image-settings.ts:73-75). The spec's §5.3 `onSettingsChange` "fires on any resolved-settings change (gesture, layer push/pop, sync)" and §5.4 `layer.onChange` fires "on writes INTO this layer (host or gesture)" — neither carries a source. Failing scenario with §5.6: `const layer = useSettingsLayer(cardSpec)` + `<Plot layers={[layer]} onSettingsChange={(vp,s) => updateSettings(s)} />`; a pan gesture writes the topmost (host) layer → `onSettingsChange` → `updateSettings` → card settings state changes → effect re-applies `layer.set(settings)` → `layer.onChange` → re-render → repeat. Every cairn-track card persists settings this way today (`useCardSettings`, e.g. HistogramCard.tsx:108-111, VisualContentCard via `useCardSeries`), so this is the default wiring, not an exotic one.
v2:bdf99058a.proposal: Put the source token in the public contract: `onSettingsChange(cb: (s, meta: { source: "gesture" | "host" | "sync" | "layer", layer?: SettingsLayer }) => void)`, and specify that `layer.set(patch)` is a no-op (no notification) when the patch is value-equal to the layer's current contents. Also answer open question 4 concretely — coalesce to one notification per frame — since pan/zoom gestures would otherwise persist at 60 Hz.

v2:bdf99058a.claim: `createSettingsLayer` has no dispose, and the underlying stores are keyed by global string id with no eviction — a long-lived dashboard that creates and destroys cards leaks one settings snapshot, one version entry, and N merge-cache entries per card, forever.
v2:bdf99058a.evidence: Layer contents live in a module-global `lastStates: Map<string, ImageSyncSettings>` only ever deleted by `clearImageSettings` (image-settings-sync.ts:236-240); `layerVersions()` entries are only ever written (`bumpLayerVersion`, :198-201); the merge cache `mergeCache.set(key, …)` keyed by `stack.join(" ")` has no delete path and the comment's claim "Bounded by the number of distinct live stacks" (:204-206) stops holding once the *host* mints layer ids per card. §5.4 says only "Unmount detaches all layers (the layer object survives …)" — nothing reclaims the store row, and §5.4's mid-stack `removeLayer` multiplies the number of distinct stack strings per viewport.
v2:bdf99058a.proposal: Add `layer.dispose()` to §5.4 (drops the store row, its version entry, and evicts every cached stack containing it), state that a disposed layer is inert if re-pushed, and give the merge cache an LRU bound. Fold this into open question 10's answer, and have `MountedPlot.unmount()` evict the mount's viewport-local layers.
